reason: The visible K-loop cost is one `sub` and conditional branch per K step in each reduction loop. Each step also loads operands and issues four FMOPA operations, so the assembly alone does not show that loop control limits throughput. The three one-entry panel proposals are effectively duplicates; rank them together. The existing panel helper and feasibility evidence make that direction executable, though pointer resets, stack lifetime, and SME state carry high correctness risk. Scratch reuse and fused packing need larger assembly changes. B-panel packing adds allocation and timed copying, while transpose fusion also changes ZA use. The three two-K loop proposals assume a two-step body, but the supplied current full512 loops consume one K step per iteration; that assumption must be checked before implementation. The transpose proposal needs a new generated shape unavailable to the implementation agent. No supplied measurements establish a gain for any proposal.
